# Evaluation and calibration

Score one candidate through a real tool backend, widen its confidence interval from calibration residuals, check validity and conformance, and explain what the numbers mean.

## Evaluator backends

Sixteen adapters behind one ABI; pass any of these as `backend`:

## Worked example

The same evaluation on all three surfaces -- library call, CHIA node, CLI:

=== "Python"

    ```python
    from flux_cli.registry import make_evaluator
    from flux_evaluator_abi import Budget, Candidate
    import flux_ir

    workload = flux_ir.load_document("core/ir/workload/examples/mlp-gemm0.yaml")
    arch = flux_ir.load_document("core/ir/architecture/examples/simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml")
    result = make_evaluator("zigzag").evaluate(
        Candidate(workload=workload, arch=arch, mapping=None),
        Budget(), frozenset({"latency_cycles", "energy_pj"}))
    print(result.metrics["latency_cycles"].value)   # 1554.0, analytic, with CI
    ```

=== "CHIA node / MCP"

    ```python
    from flux_chia_nodes import flux_evaluate

    report = flux_evaluate("zigzag", workload, arch)      # same call, JSON-safe dict
    ```

    Over MCP the tool is `flux_evaluate` with the same parameters; the
    [omni loop](../demos/omni.md) plans over exactly this surface.

=== "CLI"

    ```bash
    nix develop --command flux eval --backend zigzag \
        --workload core/ir/workload/examples/mlp-gemm0.yaml \
        --arch core/ir/architecture/examples/simple-npu-1d-v1.yaml
    ```

Swap `zigzag` for any backend in the table above; `backend_health` reports which are
usable on this machine and why the others are not.

Which evaluator backends are usable right now, and why the others are not (docs/decisions.md D156).

## calibrate

Evaluate a candidate through a named backend, then widen its confidence intervals from real calibration residual data and recompute its escalation recommendation (docs/calibration.md: "a result without a calibration id and a confidence interval is a bug").

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `str` | Evaluator backend registry name |
| `workload` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Workload IR document (inline dict). |

??? note "7 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `arch` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Architecture IR document, or omit to use the backend's own reference architecture. |
    | `mapping` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Mapping IR document, or omit to let the evaluator choose one. |
    | `metrics` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Metric names to compute, or omit for the backend's default set. |
    | `calibration_db_path` | `str` | `'flux_calibration.db'` | SQLite file of prior (predicted, reference) residual records, created if missing. |
    | `max_relative_ci_width` | `float` | `0.5` | Escalation trigger — a metric whose CI exceeds this fraction of its point value is flagged for escalation to a higher-fidelity rung. |
    | `escalate_if_recommended` | `bool` | `False` | act on the escalation advisory (docs/decisions.md D99): when the policy recommends it, buy one real `reference_backend` measurement, record its residual (the D98 flywheel), and re-calibrate before returning. |
    | `reference_backend` | `str` | `'rtl'` | which higher-fidelity rung to buy the measurement from |

## calibrate_against_generated_rtl

Measure a candidate with a *generated* design and record it as a calibration reference (docs/decisions.md D136) — narrowing that candidate's interval by evidence rather than by assumption. Measured effect on a real candidate: 24.32x wide before, 1.04x after.

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `workload` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Workload IR document (one einsum op, static bounds). |
| `arch` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Architecture IR document with one single-dim compute node. |
| `calibration_db_path` | `str` | SQLite calibration store to record into. |

??? note "4 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `backend` | `str` | `'zigzag'` | the fast model whose prediction is being calibrated. |
    | `metric` | `str` | `'latency_cycles'` | which metric to record; the generated design measures `latency_cycles`. |
    | `model` | `str` | `'qwen3.8:latest'` | Ollama model name for the tile-implementation LLM. |
    | `allow_redundant` | `bool` | `False` | record even where a reference already exists (double-counts). |

## champsim_run

Run one ChampSim simulation and report the IPC it measured.

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `config` | `dict[str, Any]` | The prefetcher configuration as plain values |
| `trace` | `str` | Path to a ChampSim trace. |

??? note "5 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `types` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | L2 prefetchers to enable |
    | `warmup_instructions` | `int` | `100000000` | Instructions before measurement starts. |
    | `simulation_instructions` | `int` | `150000000` | Measured instructions. |
    | `binary` | `str \| None` | `None` | The simulator; otherwise resolved from the environment. |
    | `timeout_s` | `float \| None` | `None` | Give up after this long. |

## characterize_memory_level

Extract one named memory-hierarchy level from a (possibly multi-level) architecture and characterize it as a standalone physical macro (docs/decisions.md D37) — the glue between this repo's real, multi-level Architecture IR documents and `evaluators/cacti`'s single-macro contract (D36): every real architecture example here has multiple `class=="memory"` nodes, but CACTI characterizes exactly one macro at a time.

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `arch` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Architecture IR document (inline dict) containing the level to characterize |
| `level` | `str` | Name of the `class=="memory"` hierarchy level to extract |
| `word_width_bits` | `int` | Bits per word for this macro — a real physical property `size_kb` alone can't determine (a 512 KiB macro could be 4096x128b or 32768x16b); none of this repo's real examples carry it yet, so it's always explicit here. |

??? note "2 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `backend` | `str` | `'cacti'` | Evaluator backend to characterize the extracted macro with — defaults to "cacti", the only backend built for this v0.1. |
    | `metrics` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Metric names to request, or omit for every metric `backend`'s adapter reports for this macro (not the generic `latency_cycles`/`energy_pj` baseline `evaluate`/`check_validity` default to — CACTI doesn't report `latency_cycles` at all, and its two most interesting numbers, `area_mm2`/`power_w`, aren't in that baseline). |

## check_validity

Evaluate a candidate, then overlay an *independently*-computed validity check onto the result (docs/gap-analysis.md G14) — merged with, not replacing, the evaluator's own self-report. `ok=True` on the returned result means both the evaluator's own check and a check that shares no code with any evaluator (declared Architecture-IR constraints, e.g. `area_mm2`/ `tdp_w` max bounds; a first-principles compute-bound latency lower-bound) found nothing wrong — not just that the evaluator says so.

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `str` | Evaluator backend registry name |
| `workload` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Workload IR document (inline dict). |

??? note "3 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `arch` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Architecture IR document, or omit to use the backend's own reference architecture. |
    | `mapping` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Mapping IR document, or omit to let the evaluator choose one. |
    | `metrics` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Metric names to compute, or omit for the backend's default set. |

## conformance_check

Check whether a fast/analytic "declared" model's *calibrated* confidence interval for a candidate actually contains a slower, more-trusted "reference" evaluator's measurement — docs/roadmap.md's exit criterion made checkable: a candidate "passes RTL conformance against its declared model within the calibrated uncertainty band."

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `workload` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Workload IR document (inline dict). |

??? note "7 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `arch` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Architecture IR document, or omit to use each backend's own reference architecture. |
    | `mapping` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Mapping IR document, or omit to let each evaluator choose one. |
    | `metrics` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Metric names to compare, or omit for the declared backend's default set. |
    | `declared_backend` | `str` | `'zigzag'` | Fast/analytic evaluator backend being checked |
    | `reference_backend` | `str` | `'rtl'` | Slower, more-trusted evaluator serving as ground truth |
    | `calibration_db_path` | `str` | `'flux_calibration.db'` | SQLite file of prior residual records used to calibrate the declared backend's confidence interval before comparing. |
    | `record_residuals` | `bool` | `False` | also record this check's own real (predicted, reference) pairs back into `calibration_db_path` — the calibration flywheel (docs/decisions.md D98): each conformance run then improves future calibrated CIs. |

## evaluate

Evaluate a candidate accelerator design through a named Flux evaluator backend.

| parameter | type | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `backend` | `str` | Evaluator backend registry name |
| `workload` | `dict[str, Any]` | Flux Workload IR document (inline dict). |

??? note "6 optional parameters"

    | parameter | type | default | what it is |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | `arch` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Architecture IR document, or omit to use the backend's own reference architecture. |
    | `mapping` | `dict[str, Any] \| None` | `None` | Flux Mapping IR document, or omit to let the evaluator choose one. |
    | `metrics` | `list[str] \| None` | `None` | Metric names to compute |
    | `wall_clock_s` | `float \| None` | `None` | Optional wall-clock budget in seconds. |
    | `usd` | `float \| None` | `None` | Optional dollar-cost budget. |
    | `result_db_path` | `str \| None` | `None` | SQLite file to warm-start against (docs/decisions.md D19) — pass the same path across calls and an identical (workload, arch, mapping) triple is served from the store instead of a real evaluator call. |
